<!-- Title: Windows/OpenCode: findRuntime reads only env.PATH (no env.Path fallback) — D11 "Git Bash not found" and every ctx_execute language fails when the env block spells it "Path" -->

### Summary

D11 shell FAIL ("Git Bash not found") plus NO_RUNTIME for every ctx_execute language on win32 OpenCode: findRuntime() reads only `env.PATH`, but OpenCode's embedded Bun runtime has a case-sensitive process.env and the Windows env block spells the variable `Path`.

### What happened

Git for Windows IS installed (`C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe` exists, git 2.54.0.windows.1), Node v24.22.3 and PowerShell 5.1 are installed and resolve in the same terminal. Yet:

```text
ctx_execute({language:"javascript", code:"..."})
→ No javascript runtime on PATH. Fix: install it or pick another language.

ctx_execute({language:"powershell", code:"..."})
→ No powershell runtime on PATH. Fix: install it or pick another language.

ctx_doctor → D11 shell | FAIL | Git Bash not found
```

Root cause — `src/core/sandbox/runtimes.ts` (line numbers from the bundled `opencode/plugin.js` of 2.1.8):

```js
// findRuntime, bundled line 20735 — no env.Path fallback:
const dirs = pathEntries(env.PATH ?? "", process.platform, path.delimiter);

// findGitBash, bundled lines 20751-20758 — depends on findRuntime:
const git2 = findRuntime(GIT_BIN, env);   // null → D11 "Git Bash not found"
```

The doctor's own probe in the same file DOES have the fallback and works:

```js
// onPath, bundled line 27870:
for (const dir of (env.PATH ?? env.Path ?? "").split(delimiter)) {
```

Same env object, two results: the report's Environment section (produced by onPath) lists
`PATH holds node: C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe` and `PATH holds git: C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe`,
while findRuntime sees an empty PATH. The only difference is the `?? env.Path` fallback.

Why `env.PATH` is undefined: OpenCode 1.19.5 runs plugins in-process under Bun 1.4.4 (D2 row). Bun's process.env is case-sensitive on Windows (Node.js's is case-insensitive). A process launched from PowerShell / cmd / VS Code integrated terminal inherits the Windows-default spelling `Path` — verified by enumerating the environment of a child process of opencode.exe: the key is `Path`, not `PATH`. So `env.PATH` → undefined, `env.Path` → the full path.

Control experiments (all verified on this machine):

1. Launch opencode from Git Bash instead (MSYS normalizes env names to uppercase): node spawned via Git Bash enumerates the key as `PATH`. This matches #1309's ctx-report (win32-x64, same Bun 1.4.4) which shows `D11 shell | PASS | Git Bash: C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe`.
2. Normalize the casing before launch, then D11's detection path works:

```powershell
$p = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','Process')
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('Path',$null,'Process')
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('PATH',$p,'Process')
opencode
```

Impact: the entire sandbox surface (ctx_execute, ctx_execute_file, ctx_batch_execute) is unusable for ALL languages on any Windows OpenCode install launched from a native Windows shell — the common case. D11's fix advice ("install Git for Windows") is misleading because Git is already installed.

Suggested fix (one line, align findRuntime with onPath):

```js
const dirs = pathEntries(env.PATH ?? env.Path ?? "", process.platform, path.delimiter);
```

or resolve the PATH key case-insensitively on win32 (match /^path$/i). Please also audit other direct `env.PATH` reads.

### Agent config

~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc at the time of the doctor run (no secrets in these entries):

```jsonc
"plugin": [
  "oh-my-opencode-slim@v3.0.7",
  "context-mode"
]
```

No context-mode MCP entry (in-process plugin, D6 PASS). Plugin root: ~/.cache/opencode/packages/context-mode@latest/node_modules/context-mode. After diagnosis the user pinned context-mode@1.0.169 (v1) as a workaround; this report concerns 2.1.8.


### Expected

- D11 PASS with detail `Git Bash: C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe`.
- `ctx_execute({language:"javascript", code:"console.log(1)"})` returns `1\n` (2 B) instead of the NO_RUNTIME error.
- Runtime resolution on Windows must not depend on the casing of the PATH environment variable name.

### Steps

1. Windows 10/11 x64. Install Git for Windows (default location), Node 24, and OpenCode: `npm i -g opencode-ai`.
2. Fresh project: `mkdir fresh && cd fresh && git init`.
3. `opencode plugin add context-mode` (resolves 2.1.8).
4. Launch `opencode` from PowerShell or the VS Code integrated terminal (NOT Git Bash). The process env block spells the path variable `Path`.
5. Call ctx_doctor → `D11 shell | FAIL | Git Bash not found`, while the report's Environment section lists `PATH holds node: C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe` and `PATH holds git: C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe`.
6. Call ctx_execute with language javascript (or powershell) → `No javascript runtime on PATH` / `No powershell runtime on PATH`, although both resolve in the same terminal.
7. Control: exit, launch `opencode` from Git Bash → D11 PASS and ctx_execute works.

### Environment

- context-mode 2.1.8 (92c1ad2); install route: opencode plugin add context-mode (in-process plugin)
- Agent: OpenCode 1.19.5 (npm opencode-ai); plugins run under embedded Bun 1.4.4
- OS: Windows 10 x64 (build 18362), win32-x64
- Node: v24.22.3 installed at C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe; doctor prints "Node v26.3.0" (Bun's compat version)
- Launch shell: PowerShell 5.1 (VS Code integrated terminal); doctor detects shell C:\windows\system32\cmd.exe
- git 2.54.0.windows.1 at C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe; Git Bash exists at C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe
- Env var spelling: `Path` (verified in a child process of opencode.exe); `env.PATH` is undefined under Bun
- PATH holds node: C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe; PATH holds git: C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe (via onPath's env.Path fallback)
- Filed by: user via OpenCode agent
